name: Chicago double-dose algebra
whyItIsMissing: The dossier has Algebra for All but not the distinct extended-instruction policy with a stronger causal design and long-run outcomes.
theoryOfAction: Require an additional daily algebra-support period for ninth graders below a pre-policy test-score threshold.
targetPopulation: Chicago ninth graders with below-median prior math scores during the policy period.
evaluationDesign: Regression discontinuity and longitudinal administrative follow-up.
keyCaveat: Effects depend on the threshold rule, implementation, peer grouping, and a single-district setting.

primarySource.title: Doubling Up? Understanding the Long-Term Effects of Ninth-grade Algebra Reform on College Persistence and Graduation

name: Principal Pipeline Initiative
whyItIsMissing: Leadership is not represented as a discrete initiative despite a multi-district evaluation with achievement, retention, and cost findings.
theoryOfAction: Strengthen leader standards, preparation, selective hiring, evaluation, and on-the-job support as a coherent district system.
targetPopulation: Schools receiving newly placed principals in participating districts.
evaluationDesign: Multi-district matched comparison with implementation and cost analysis.
keyCaveat: The package was evaluated as a system; individual components cannot be credited separately.

primarySource.title: Principal Pipelines: A Feasible, Affordable, and Effective Way for Districts to Improve Schools

name: Dual-language immersion programs
whyItIsMissing: Dual language is a continuum topic but lacks a program-level initiative record tied to lottery evidence and bilingualism outcomes.
theoryOfAction: Deliver academic and literacy instruction in English and a partner language over multiple years.
targetPopulation: Elementary and middle-grade students participating in immersion programs.
evaluationDesign: Lottery-based evidence reviewed by the What Works Clearinghouse.
keyCaveat: Results vary by program model, language pair, time horizon, student selection, and whether biliteracy is treated as an outcome.

primarySource.title: Effects of Dual-Language Immersion Programs on Student Achievement: Evidence from Lottery Data

name: Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System (EWIMS)
whyItIsMissing: The dossier covers attendance interventions but not the distinct randomized early-warning-system model that uses attendance, behavior, and course performance together.
theoryOfAction: Use school teams and data routines to identify students at risk and assign supports before students fall further off track.
targetPopulation: First- and second-year high school students in participating schools.
evaluationDesign: Cluster randomized controlled trial across 73 high schools.
keyCaveat: The first-year study found risk-indicator improvements but no detectable effect on credit accumulation, and implementation was challenging.

primarySource.title: Getting students on track for graduation: Impacts of the Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System after one year

name: San Francisco ethnic studies curriculum pilot
whyItIsMissing: Culturally relevant curriculum is absent despite a policy-relevant regression-discontinuity study with large high-school engagement outcomes.
theoryOfAction: Offer a culturally relevant ninth-grade course to students assigned around an eighth-grade GPA threshold.
targetPopulation: Ninth-grade students in participating San Francisco high schools near the assignment threshold.
keyCaveat: The study is tied to a particular pilot, threshold, and fidelity context; it should not stand in for every ethnic studies implementation.

primarySource.title: The Causal Effects of Cultural Relevance: Evidence from an Ethnic Studies Curriculum

name: Comprehensive teacher induction
whyItIsMissing: The teacher-workforce collection has coaching and evaluation, but not a major randomized test of structured novice-teacher induction with largely null findings.
theoryOfAction: Provide full-time mentoring, mentoring training, professional development, and observation opportunities to beginning teachers.
targetPopulation: Beginning elementary teachers in districts not already offering comprehensive induction.
evaluationDesign: School-level randomized controlled trial across 17 districts.
keyCaveat: One-year induction had no student-achievement impact; a later positive subset result for two-year induction requires careful interpretation.

primarySource.title: Impacts of Comprehensive Teacher Induction: Final Results from a Randomized Controlled Study

name: Community Eligibility Provision / universal free school meals
whyItIsMissing: The dossier is thin on universal service policies whose most direct outcomes are family resources, food security, participation, and stigma rather than test scores.
theoryOfAction: Offer meals to all students in eligible high-poverty schools without individual meal applications.
targetPopulation: Students and households in schools eligible for the Community Eligibility Provision.
keyCaveat: This initial source does not establish student academic effects; add education-outcome evidence before positioning it as an academic intervention.

primarySource.title: The Effect of Free School Meals on Household Food Purchases: Evidence from the Community Eligibility Provision
